entries.question: Which issues does this Mission fix, and which half of #5099 is in scope?

entries.final_answer: Reuse the existing per-mission feature_status_lock (keyed on the Mission directory name under the git common dir) as the one Mission write lock; add one checkout-wide claim lock only for the single_branch occupancy check, modelled on the verdict-save queue. No parallel per-file locks. Operator brief + #5819/#5804 triage (lock-held, tail-verified rollback as one fix).
entries.question: Which lock guards Mission-file mutation: a new mechanism or the existing per-mission status lock?

entries.final_answer: Only rows it appended itself in the same lock hold, never a row already committed at HEAD, never when the log shrank or the tail does not parse; on refusal it leaves the log intact and says so loudly. Start from PR #4072's status/rollback.py design (operator ruling on #5819, 2026-10-07).

entries.final_answer: implement claims in a single_branch shared checkout stay REFUSED (existing WRITE_CHECKOUT_OCCUPIED, now atomic); review/implement in a workspace another actor holds in_progress/in_review get an advisory warning only (blocking refusal is #3129's product decision, per #5099 triage).
